records.claim: The domestic Solar PV grant is EUR 700 per kWp up to 2 kWp, then EUR 200 for every additional kWp up to 4 kWp, paid pro rata.
The maximum domestic Solar PV grant is EUR 1,800 in 2026.
records.notes: Stated per calendar year. Withholds itself on 2027-01-01 with no code change. A 2027 value must be VERIFIED, never inferred.

records.claim: The Government plans to reduce the grant by up to EUR 300 each year as panel costs fall.
records.notes: ANNOUNCED, not in force. Must never be applied as a current value. Context only.

records.claim: The grant is due to end in 2029.
records.notes: ANNOUNCED. Not an expiry on any current record.

records.claim: The home must have been built and occupied before 2021.
The grant is not open to homes with previous funding for solar PV at that MPRN, whoever claimed it.
records.notes: Applies across ownership changes. A previous owner's claim uses it.

records.claim: The home needs an MPRN.
Eligible applicants are all homeowners including private landlords, owner management companies, and approved housing bodies.
Once approved there are 8 months to complete the works and submit the documentation, after which the grant expires.
The installer applies to ESB Networks before the system is installed; the application usually takes at least 4 weeks.
A post-works BER assessment is required before the grant is paid.
Allow 4 to 6 weeks for the grant payment once the documents and the published BER are in.
A 0% VAT rate applies to the supply and installation of solar panels on private dwellings.
Rooftop solar panels on houses do not require planning permission.
There is no rooftop area limit on houses, whether or not the house is inside a Solar Safeguarding Zone.
records.notes: Solar Safeguarding Zones apply to every building class EXCEPT houses. A prior PlotNua reading of this was wrong and was corrected on the live Discovery on 14 September 2026.

records.claim: Restrictions still apply to protected structures and homes in an Architectural Conservation Area, and the exemption carries conditions such as a minimum distance from the edge of the roof.
SEAI does not approve, guarantee, or warranty a company or their works.
records.notes: Quoted verbatim from SEAI. WITHHOLD rather than downgrade: if the wording changes we must stop quoting it, not soften it.

records.claim: A smart meter gives access to smart and time-of-use tariff options.
Having a smart meter installed does not mean being on a time-of-use tariff; that is a separate choice with the supplier.
records.source_title: CRU Chairperson, quoted in ESB smart meter release
records.notes: The most common homeowner misunderstanding in this journey.

records.claim: Over two million smart meters are installed and more than four out of five households have one.
records.source_title: Over two million smart meters installed nationwide
records.notes: POPULATION STATISTIC. logic_safe=false by design: it must never be used to infer that a particular home has a meter. Both figures are floors, and the rollout continues.

records.claim: There is no SEAI grant for home battery storage.
records.notes: A NEGATIVE claim. Re-checked on a 6-month cycle because a stale negative costs a homeowner money as surely as a stale positive.

records.claim: Electricity from a renewable source stored in a battery and used, or exported later, is still treated as renewable.
An AC-connected battery is considered a microgenerator for ESB Networks purposes.
records.source_title: Quick User Guide: Microgeneration & Smart Battery Energy Storage (DOC-301121-HFX)

records.claim: ESB Networks is notified before the battery is installed.
records.source_title: Quick User Guide: Microgeneration & Smart Battery Energy Storage (DOC-301121-HFX)

records.claim: An AC-connected battery is listed on the ESB Networks NC6 application with its rated output, within the microgeneration thresholds.
records.source_title: Conditions Governing the Connection and Operation of Micro-Generation (DTIS-230206-BRL v6.1)
records.notes: homeowner_safe=false: NC6, amps and kVA are installer vocabulary. The reveal says ESB Networks is told first; the form is detail. logic_safe=false: the frozen V1 journey does not gate on the threshold, so marking it engine-facing would be dead surface.

records.claim: The AC system must be tested and certified by a Registered Electrical Contractor, and a Safe Electric certificate provided.
records.source_title: Quick User Guide: Microgeneration & Smart Battery Energy Storage (DOC-301121-HFX)

records.claim: Type-test certification to I.S. EN 50549-1 and a protection-settings confirmation certificate are required, and copies are given to the customer.
records.source_title: Conditions Governing the Connection and Operation of Micro-Generation (DTIS-230206-BRL v6.1)

records.claim: Inverter or aggregate capacity determines which connection route applies; requirements are not identical for every installation.
records.source_title: Conditions Governing the Connection and Operation of Micro-Generation (DTIS-230206-BRL v6.1)
records.notes: RESIDUAL LIMITATION, recorded and NOT generalised: the reviewed ESB Networks material does not establish the treatment of a battery genuinely incapable of exporting or operating in parallel with the distribution network. records.claim: Every electricity supplier must pay for eligible electricity exported to the grid.
records.notes: The scheme is styled INTERIM Clean Export Guarantee (CRU21131). The word interim is itself a standing review signal.

records.claim: With a smart meter and a processed NC6 or NC7, the supplier pays for every metered unit exported.
Where the home is eligible for a smart meter and waiting, payment is not made while waiting and begins when the meter is installed.
records.notes: Not separated from state C at the surface: meter eligibility is ESB Networks' determination, not a fact the homeowner holds.

records.claim: Where the home is not yet eligible for a smart meter, the supplier pays on a calculated export quantity instead.
records.notes: The regulator's term is 'deemed export quantity'. The journey says 'a calculated amount' — same meaning, no jargon.

records.claim: Where a smart meter has been offered and refused, the home is not eligible for export payment.
records.notes: The only FALSE in the journey. An UNKNOWN meter answer must never resolve here.

records.claim: Without the NC6 or NC7 processed by ESB Networks, the supplier will not pay for exported electricity.
Each supplier sets its own export rate; the rates are open to competition and are not regulated.
records.notes: NO RATE IS STORED IN THIS MANIFEST, at any time, for any supplier.

records.claim: Where the home is eligible, ESB Networks endeavours to install a smart meter within four months of a processed NC6, and a prioritised installation can be requested.
The first EUR 400 a year of microgeneration income is exempt from income tax.
records.notes: Withholds itself on 2029-01-01. Any replacement must be VERIFIED, never inferred.

records.claim: To qualify, the home must have solar panels, have been built before 2021, have an MPRN, and be registered with an electricity supplier. No minimum BER applies.
